newsitem.title: INDIA: India communists threaten government on insurance.
newsitem.headline: India communists threaten government on insurance.

text.p: The Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M) has threatened to quit Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's coalition if it pursues efforts to privatise the insurance industry, the Economic Times said on Saturday.
The centre-left United Front government said last year it would set up an independent Insurance Regulatory Authority (IRA) to bring private capital into the state insurance monopoly.

"If the government wants to rule without 33 members of parliament, fine. Then it can try to enact the IRA legislation to open up the sector despite our protests," CPI-M spokesman Prakash Karat was quoted as saying.
A party spokesman was unavailable for comment.
The CPI-M is a member of the coalition but has no ministerial posts. Its strength is not enough to topple Deve Gowda on its own.

The 13-party United Front (UF), which commands the support of 190 lawmakers including members of the CPI-M in the 545-member parliament, relies mainly on the Congress party, which controls 140 votes, for a majority.

But the CPI-M played a crucial role in setting up the coalition last year when it helped rally regional and leftist parties to join and keep the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) from power.

The communists also criticised the recommendations of a government pay commission, which said in a report submitted on Thursday that the government should abolish 350,000 existing jobs and aim to slash a million jobs over the next decade.
"The UF government cannot accept this basic recommendation which goes against its commitment to generate more employment," the CPI-M said in a statement.
The party also attacked what it said was a move by the commission to provide more benefits for higher government officials compared to juniors.
Last month it criticised moves to add nine more industries to a list of those in which foreign investors are allowed to hold 51 percent equity.
